You are clustering code review findings from the same PR. For each PAIR below, decide whether the two findings describe the SAME underlying issue — same root cause in the same code location. Different wording is fine. A finding about a DIFFERENT defect in the same file or function is NOT the same issue. Severity or aspect differences of the same root cause ARE the same issue.


For THIS scoring pass, duplicate equivalence is stricter than sharing a root cause.
You must compare the COMPLETE MATERIAL CLAIMS, including mechanism, triggering
conditions, execution path, and consequence. The same line or broad concern does
not establish equivalence. A report of wrong-category selection, a case/rename
mismatch, a crash, and a silent fallback are different claims even at one lookup.
An inactive/unbound API concern and an alleged active user-facing failure differ.
A compound report with an additional material claim does NOT equal its subset.
Differences only in wording, severity, or hedging do not create separate claims.
If the claimed mechanisms, triggers or consequences conflict, or one report adds
an unsupported/different material factual claim, return same=false. You are NOT
verifying which claim is true; do not repair or reinterpret either report to make
them match. If unsure whether their full claims are equivalent, return false.

For every numbered pair, extract what A and B actually CLAIM into mechanism,
trigger and consequence. Then list material_differences and give your equivalence
verdict, confidence and reason. same=true requires no material differences.

PAIR 17:
A: saveChanges calls this.get('embedding').update({}) with an empty payload, so the save button wired into the update endpoint persists nothing and depends entirely on the no-op server handler to appear to succeed. Admins clicking any embedding-level save in the UI silently lose their action; the next change to this controller that assumes update persists state will be built on a path that provably writes nothing.
B: Admin::EmbeddingController#update never reads params or mutates @embedding; it re-renders the fetch_embedding snapshot unchanged, so the PUT /admin/customize/embedding endpoint the frontend's saveChanges action calls is a silent no-op. An admin who changes embedding-level settings and clicks save gets a success response while nothing is persisted; combined with the client controller sending update({}), the update route exists purely to satisfy the adapter and stores no data.

A: TopicEmbed.import behavioral change with no matching host is untested: category now comes from EmbeddableHost.record_for_host(url).try(:category_id), but the unmatched-host case (category nil → PostCreator default instead of previous SiteSetting.embed_category) has no spec coverage
B: TopicEmbed.import with no matching host record now creates the topic with no category since the global embed_category setting was removed; callers like feed-polling imports previously landed in the configured embed category — behavior change with no test pinning the no-match path

PAIR 19:
A: db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb:25 — legacy host_list values are inserted raw with `VALUES ('#{h}', ...)`, which skips the model's before_validation normalization, so hosts the old `allows_embeddable_host?` accepted (`http://discourse.org`, `https://example.com/1234`, trailing `\r`/whitespace, blank lines) never match `where("lower(host) = ?", uri.host)` and existing embeds start getting "invalid referer host" after upgrade (and a quote in a value breaks the SQL) (P1, conf 75)
B: db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb:25 — Raw string interpolation into INSERT: a host containing `'` aborts the migration, and hosts saved as `http://foo.com` or with trailing `\r`/path are inserted verbatim (model normalization is bypassed) so `lower(host) = uri.host` never matches and embedding silently stops working post-migration.

PAIR 20:
A: The INSERT interpolates each raw setting value without the scheme/path stripping the old allows_embeddable_host? applied and without the model's before_validation, so entries like 'http://eviltrout.com' or 'https://example.com/1234' — both exercised as working values by the removed specs — are stored verbatim and can never match record_for_host's lower(host) = uri.host comparison. Upgraded sites whose working host entries carried a scheme or path end up with rows that authorize nothing (embedding silently denied for those hosts); a stored value containing a single quote additionally makes the INSERT raise a SQL syntax error that aborts the migration.
B: The migration's raw INSERT copies legacy embeddable_hosts entries verbatim, applying neither the model's scheme/path normalization (which Fabricate-based specs prove runs on every normal save) nor any SQL escaping. A legacy entry like 'http://eviltrout.com' — which the old SiteSetting.allows_embeddable_host? explicitly matched by stripping the scheme — is stored as-is and can never satisfy record_for_host's lower(host) = uri.host comparison, so those sites' embedded comments start failing with 'invalid referer host' after the upgrade until an admin manually re-saves each host; additionally a legacy value containing a single quote aborts the migration with a SQL syntax error.
